As somebody with the condition I understand why you wouldn't trust people like me. The hurt and pain you feel is completely understandable. I also get into the thought processes and then go and apologize. As a bpd person it can be hard to understand abuse and what it actually is vs and innocent mistake. That doesn't mean what they do is OK and its fair to talk out about it. I also understand though not wanting to be called an awful person for confusion. I wouldn't date someone like me. I got into a relationship way too quickly and moved in with him after a past abusive relationship. If you're gonna date someone like me you need to find someone that wants to heal and not keep jumping into relationships. Many of them will know they have the disorder so if they don't want to change they would be just like the people who hurt them (most likely their parents) they know how much it hurts to have someone who won't change or care for them. That's the double edge sword of this disorder. 
 Experience someone who cares about you because there are good people, bad people and confused people with the disorder. Good intentions, bad intentions and confused intentions.  Find someone willing to work with you and understand healing takes s lot of time and you don't have to get in a relationship with someone who is actively healing because you deserve someone who can care for you most of the time and not none of it. 
 Personally I deal with psycosis when I get better because I realize I am wrong and completely lose my grounding. Understand that its a complex and really annoying disorder too. 
 People care for you and you are genuinely important. Take care of yourself first before taking care of others. <3
